description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='19/07/2022' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='DD/MM/YYYY' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. This program opens no file and is reached by no JCL, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57, the 88-level feedback tokens at L62-L70 and the group move at L122; they are never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible here, one blocker being this program's own PROCEDURE DIVISION USING at L88 and another being the absence of any Language Environment CEEDAYS to call at L116. Arm 1 of the EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149, reached a second time under a SECOND mask. FC-INVALID-DATE carries the 88-level VALUE X'0000000000000000' (L62) and is - despite its name - the SUCCESS token: the eight-byte token decodes as halfword SEVERITY 0 and halfword MSG-NO 0 (L72-L73), which is why WS-SEVERITY-N prints 0000 at offset 0, WS-MSG-NO-N prints 0000 at offset 15 and RETURN-CODE is 0 rather than the 3 every named error returns. The arm moves 'Date is valid' (L130) into WS-RESULT PIC X(15), so offsets 20-34 hold those 13 characters and the 2 spaces the alphanumeric receiver pads on the right. Running arm 1 again under a different picture string is what proves WS-DATE-FMT at offset 66 is echoed verbatim from LS-DATE-FORMAT rather than hard-coded, and that the mask genuinely drives field order: the day now precedes the year and the delimiter is a solidus. It is the same calendar day as case01, so any difference between the two lines can only come from the mask. Offsets 45-54 are not the date. L122 MOVE WS-DATE-TO-TEST TO WS-DATE is a GROUP move, and the group begins with Vstring-length PIC S9(4) BINARY, so the leftmost ten bytes of the group are two binary bytes - the halfword 10 that L105-L106 set from LENGTH OF LS-DATE, which is the DECLARED width of a PIC X(10) item and therefore always ten, rendered in this file as the two explicit escapes for 0x00 and 0x0A so the pair reads as the halfword 0x000A and not as a newline in the data - followed by only the first eight characters, 19/07/20. Under this mask the two discarded digits are the tail of the year, where case01's YYYY-MM-DD loses the day instead. L122 overwrites what L107-L108 placed there; that is the program's own observable output and is preserved verbatim, not repaired.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '19/07/2022' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'DD/MM/YYYY', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
